notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 81. My one attempt to fetch the commentary pages was blocked by a tool-call limit before any page loaded, so I didn't read any sources.

You asked me to report only what the pages say and to leave out anything I couldn't find. With nothing read, that leaves nothing for any verse. I didn't fill the gaps from memory, because that would break your rules and give you points with no real URLs behind them.

If you ask again, I'll start with these pages:

- **Verse by verse:** enduringword.com (Psalm 81) and the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages on biblehub.com
- **Methodist:** Wesley's notes on studylight.org
- **Modern scholarship:** netbible.org notes on difficult points like the "unfamiliar language" in v. 5, Meribah in v. 7 and "feign obedience" in v. 15
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine's sermon on this psalm at newadvent.org. Older Catholic Bibles number it Psalm 80, so I'll search under that number too.
- **Where traditions differ:** pages on v. 12 ("I gave them up to their stubborn hearts"), which touches the Reformed and Wesleyan debate over God's hardening and human freedom, and on v. 10 ("Open wide your mouth"), a verse popular in prosperity teaching
- **Lutheran and other views:** gotquestions.org, desiringgod.org and lcms.org

The finished notes will go verse by verse ("v. 4: ...") with a URL after every point, and they'll skip anything the sources don't cover.
